runtime.standing: identity only: this names the archive a pair loads; MAESTRO-M0-RUNTIME-BUILD and MAESTRO-M0-RUNTIME are receipts under Plans/integration-completion/evidence/, never this file

location.rule: obtain the archive by archive.sha256 and verify the sidecar and sha512; the directory is where the packager lands it

receipts.rule: a counterpart adapter records qualifiedAgainst.maestroRuntimeSha256 = archive.sha256 in its own pin, read by scripts/mega-maestro-pair.mjs; nothing an adapter records is written here, so qualification cannot change the archive it names

conformance.standing: a public, secret-free description of what the managed facade of library/index.js answers a consumer, read by a counterpart adapter as the behavior it maps and proven over the public exports by src/__tests__/integration/mega-maestro/conformance.test.ts; independent of sibling private source and of the acceptance artifacts under Plans/mega-maestro-rc/; it qualifies nothing (no pair, no provider, no lease): the sink it drives is a declared double and the runs it names never start a process

host.rule: a host composes the facade over its own run journal, context verifier, authority, binding, agent repository and turn port; a consumer never composes it, it calls the ManagedApi the host exposes (in process, or over the host bridge as managed.*)

consumer.negotiate: negotiate(offer) takes no context: { supportedVersions, required, optional? }
consumer.envelope: { context, input }; the HOST stamps peer after admitting the caller, a caller never names it
consumer.context: ManagedOperationContext: contractVersion, installation, origin, actor, delegation, identity, policyRevision, workflow, traceId, requestedCapabilities
consumer.validate: managedContextProblems(context) is the structural check a consumer can run itself; whether the attribution is true is the host verifier's decision

correlation: every ManagedOperationResult carries the requestId of the context it answers, a refusal included; a malformed context is answered with the requestId read off it, or empty
an accepted submit answers run.runId = identity.runId when the peer named one, else a run id the host minted; rootRunId defaults to the run id; run.attemptId = identity.attemptId
a replayed submit (same idempotencyKey, same content.sha256) answers the first run with its latest attempt id and reaches no sink
the same idempotencyKey with other content, or a runId the journal already holds, is denied idempotency-conflict
inspect, cancel and interrupt address a run by runId; a run the journal does not hold is denied not-found

semantics.denied: a decision: unauthenticated (no verifier for the transport, or an attribution the verifier refuses), invalid-input, capability-unsupported (the context did not request the capability of the operation), not-found, context-mismatch, idempotency-conflict, policy-denied
semantics.unsupported: no code path on this host (policy.status without a host adapter, events.resume without an event journal)
semantics.unavailable: no decision could be obtained (the run journal could not be written, the sink has no authority); nothing started
semantics.unknown: a real answer: the host cannot say whether the effect happened; a replay of an unknown run is answered unknown and not resent; cancel of an unknown run, or of a run the sink no longer holds, answers outcome unknown

pong.text: Reply with the single word: pong.

ping.text: Reply with the single word: ping.

negotiation.note: the facade negotiates at the locally-verified minimum, so on this build only capabilities.negotiate activates; the run operations are implemented and answer when a verified context requested them, but a peer that REQUIRES one is refused rather than quietly downgraded

operations.sink: the declared turn-port double of the fixture: send is what the host's sendManaged answers the facade, then the journal marks runAgentTurn would write before the facade re-reads the run, cancel what cancelRun answers; a step with a sink reaches it exactly once, a step without one must not reach it
operations.defaults: identity defaults to requestId req:<id>, idempotencyKey idem:<id>, attemptId att:<id>, runId null; caps to the capability of op; a submit input to host.defaultSubmit with content named by key (an object names the text and the sha256 by separate keys); origin headless, delegation direct, traceId trace:<id>; expect is matched as a subset of the result and requestId is checked on every step
